ic_name: MIPI DSI v1.01.00 (Display Serial Interface, MIPI Alliance)
protocol_type: Packet-based half-duplex display-traffic protocol on top of source-synchronous DDR D-PHY. Two transaction styles coexist: (a) command/parameter transactions (Command Mode) using DCS and Generic Read/Write Short/Long Packets, and (b) real-time pixel-stream transactions (Video Mode) using Sync Event Short Packets + Packed/Loosely-Packed RGB Long Packets + Blanking/Null Long Packets.

channels.name: Clock+ / Clock-
channels.direction: host → peripheral (HS); idle LP-11 between bursts
channels.purpose: Differential DDR Clock Lane; sourced exclusively by host.

channels.name: Data0+ / Data0-
channels.direction: host → peripheral (HS); bidirectional in LP for Command Mode; carries all reverse-direction LP traffic
channels.purpose: Differential Data Lane 0; carries Short / Long Packets and is the only lane used for reverse direction (BTA + ACK + read response + TE).

channels.name: Data1..3 (optional)
channels.purpose: Additional unidirectional Data Lanes for higher forward bandwidth; bytes interleaved round-robin.

packet_classes.purpose: Command Mode commands, Video Mode Sync Events, Generic Short Read/Write Request, DCS Short Write/Read, Set Maximum Return Packet Size.
packet_classes.header_layout: DI (1 byte) + Data0 (1 byte) + Data1 (1 byte) + ECC (1 byte) = 4 bytes.

packet_classes.purpose: Pixel streams, generic blocks of host-to-peripheral data, blanking padding, DCS Long Write.
packet_classes.header_layout: DI (1 byte) + Word Count LS (1 byte) + Word Count MS (1 byte) + ECC (1 byte) = 32-bit Packet Header.
packet_classes.payload_layout: WC bytes of data; LSB-first within each byte; pixel format may impose multiple-of-N constraint on WC.
packet_classes.footer_layout: 16-bit Packet Footer = CRC-16 polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1, init 0xFFFF, LSB-first; covers payload only. For zero-length payload, Footer = 0xFFFF.
members: 0x19 Blanking Packet, no data (Video Mode blanking interval padding)
0x2E Packed Pixel Stream 18-bit RGB666 Loosely Packed (three bytes per pixel)

packet_classes.purpose: Acknowledge / error report / short read responses, EoTp.
packet_classes.header_layout: DI (1 byte) + Byte 1 + Byte 2 + ECC (1 byte) = 4 bytes.
members: 0x02 Acknowledge and Error Report (Byte 1 = Error[7:0], Byte 2 = Error[15:8])

packet_classes.header_layout: DI + WC LS + WC MS + ECC + payload + 16-bit Checksum.

processor_sourced_long_packets.name: DCS Long Write / write_LUT Command Packet
Loosely Packed Pixel Stream, 18-bit RGB 6-6-6 (three bytes per pixel)

peripheral_sourced_short_packets.name: Generic Short READ Response, 1 byte returned
Generic Short READ Response, 2 bytes returned
DCS Short READ Response, 1 byte returned
DCS Short READ Response, 2 bytes returned

peripheral_sourced_long_packets.name: Generic Long READ Response (with optional Checksum)
DCS Long READ Response (with optional Checksum)

data_types_enum.reserved_and_do_not_use: DT codes with DT[3:0] = 0b0000 or 0b1111 shall NOT be used. Other unspecified codes are Reserved. The DT encoding guarantees at least one 0-1 or 1-0 transition in DT[3:0].

header_ecc_field.structure: Hamming-modified (24,8): 6 parity bits over 24 data bits (DI + WC LS + WC MS) packed into ECC[5:0]; P6 and P7 are unused and shall be 0 by transmitter; receiver shall ignore P6/P7 and force them to 0 before processing.
header_ecc_field.detection_capability: Double-bit header error — detected; packet shall be dropped; peripheral sets ECC Multi-Bit (Error Report bit 9).

payload_crc_field.shift_direction: LSB-first (per DSI v1.01.00 Annex B reference implementation gsCRC16GenerationCode = 0x8408 = bit-reversed 0x1021)
payload_crc_field.covers: Long Packet payload bytes only (NOT the header).

transaction_phases: HS Entry: LP-11 → LP-01 → LP-00 → HS-0 → Sync 8'b00011101 → HS payload (per D-PHY).
Packet Stream: one or more concatenated Short / Long Packets (DI → WC → ECC → payload → Checksum for Long).
Optional EoTp: Short Packet DT=0x08, VC=0, Data=0x0F0F, ECC=0x01 appended at end of every HS transmission when enabled.
Optional BTA: LP Escape Mode handover from host to peripheral; peripheral transmits LP response packets; peripheral hands bus back to host with its own BTA.
Optional TE: peripheral, holding the bus after a BTA-without-command, sends LP Escape trigger 0x5D (LSB-first 10111010) then returns bus to host.

addressing.device_address: None at the protocol layer; DSI is normatively point-to-point (host ↔ one peripheral). Multi-peripheral implementations may overload VC[1:0] but are out of normative scope.
addressing.VC_role: Time-multiplex multiple logical streams or peripherals onto the same physical DSI Link.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: No per-packet ACK / NAK / retry on HS payload; integrity is end-to-end via ECC (1-bit correct / 2-bit detect on header) and CRC-16 (payload).

Following a non-Read command with BTA asserted, peripheral responds with Acknowledge Trigger Message (single byte 0x21 in escape mode) if no errors stored, or with Acknowledge and Error Report Short Packet (DT=0x02) if any error bits are set.

Following a Read Request with BTA, peripheral responds with the requested DCS / Generic Short/Long Read Response packet (with optional Checksum); if only a single-bit ECC error was detected and corrected, the Read Response is followed by a 4-byte Acknowledge and Error Report packet in the same LP transmission.
Multi-bit ECC error on a request: peripheral does NOT execute the command and shall send only a 4-byte Acknowledge and Error Report (no read data) with ECC Multi-Bit flag set.

Errors accumulate in the peripheral's Error Register across multiple transmissions until the next BTA; only a single Acknowledge and Error Report shall be returned regardless of how many transmissions preceded the BTA.
EoTp (when enabled) does not replace D-PHY EoT sequence — both are present per packet.
Set Maximum Return Packet Size (0x37) constrains read responses; default is 1 byte at power-on / reset.
endian_policy: Bytes traverse the interface LSB-first; multi-byte fields (WC, Checksum, read-response 2-byte data) transmit least-significant byte first.
